message.content:
In a standard poker hand the “most hearts” you can hold is simply the number of cards in that hand:

| Game | Cards per hand | Max hearts a single player can have |
|------|----------------|-------------------------------------|
| 5‑card poker (e.g., Five‑Card Draw) | 5 | **5** (a flush of hearts) |
| Texas Hold’em (2 hole cards + 5 community cards) | 7 | **7** (a 7‑card flush of hearts) |

So the player who actually holds that hand—i.e., a flush of hearts in a 5‑card hand or a 7‑card flush in Texas Hold’em—has the highest possible number of hearts in that particular game. If you’re looking at a different variant (e.g., Omaha, Seven‑Card Stud), the same logic applies: the maximum hearts equals the number of cards dealt to that player.
